# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Brill_2016_midazolam"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Brill_2016_midazolam"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/psp4.12048> (open access, PMC4728292)

**The second midazolam inter-compartmental clearance is not a fitted value.**
The authors' NONMEM code (Supplementary Information S3) estimates it
(`Q12 = THETA(18)`), but its final estimate is printed nowhere in the article
or its supplements. The model fixes it at 0.5 L/min, the initial estimate in
that code. It governs the slow terminal phase of midazolam, so simulated
midazolam concentrations late after a dose, and quantities that depend on
them (terminal half-life, AUC extrapolation), are uncertain. See
"Assumptions and deviations".

This cohort has two other analyses in the literature: occasion 1 (the day of
surgery) pooled with healthy volunteers in Brill 2014 (packaged as
`Brill_2014_midazolam`), and both occasions, midazolam only, in Brill 2015
(doi:10.1007/s11095-015-1752-9). The present model adds the CYP3A metabolite
1-OH-midazolam and separates first-pass metabolism into a gut-wall and a
hepatic part, so that the effect of surgery on hepatic and intestinal CYP3A
activity can be estimated separately.

# Population

Twenty morbidly obese adults (12 F / 8 M; age 26-57 years; body weight
112-186 kg, mean 144.4 kg; BMI 40-68 kg/m^2) undergoing laparoscopic
Roux-en-Y gastric bypass or sleeve gastrectomy received 7.5 mg oral
midazolam and, 160 +/- 48 min later, 5 mg IV midazolam on the day of
surgery. Eighteen of them (11 F / 7 M; 62-138 kg, mean 98.3 kg; mean weight
loss 44.5 kg) were studied again one year later with the same design. A mean
of 22 blood samples per patient and occasion were assayed for midazolam and
1-OH-midazolam (Brill 2016 Methods and Table 2). The same information is in
the model's `population` metadata.

# Model structure

The gut wall, portal vein and liver are assumed to be at quasi-steady state
(Supplementary Information S2), so they appear as algebraic concentrations
rather than ODE states. With `fub`, `fu_gut` the unbound fractions, `qh` the
hepatic blood flow and `qvi` the villous blood flow:

* hepatic extraction (well-stirred, Eq. 1): `eh = cl_int_h * fub / (qh + cl_int_h * fub)`;
* gut-wall extraction (Qgut model, Eqs. 3-4): `qgut = qvi * cl_per / (qvi + cl_per)`,
  `egut = cl_int_g * fu_gut / (qgut + cl_int_g * fu_gut)`;
* the same two relations for 1-OH-midazolam, with `qvi` in place of `qgut`
  (Eq. 6);
* oral midazolam leaves the fifth transit compartment into the gut wall;
  the fraction `1 - egut` passes to the portal vein and the fraction
  `egut` is converted to 1-OH-midazolam in the gut wall;
* the liver receives portal-vein and hepatic-artery blood; the fraction
  `eh` of midazolam entering the liver is converted to 1-OH-midazolam, which
  is in turn subject to hepatic (and, for metabolite formed in the gut wall,
  gut-wall) extraction before it reaches the systemic circulation.

Hepatic blood flow is the allometric scenario 1 of Table 1,
`qh = 3.75 * WT^0.75 / 60` L/min, with portal-vein, hepatic-artery,
intestinal, mucosal and villous flows as fixed fractions of it. Both
analytes are reported as blood concentrations in ng/mL; 1-OH-midazolam is
expressed in midazolam-mass equivalents because the authors' code applies no
molecular-weight conversion.

# Derived quantities

## Published ratios and hepatic blood flows

The paper reports a 1.52-fold higher CLint,H after surgery, and quotes the
hepatic blood flow of each scenario for the median patient before (144 kg)
and after surgery (98 kg). Scenarios 2 and 3 are not packaged (the paper
reports only their CLint,H values), but their blood flows follow from
Table 1.

```{r derived}
mod <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Brill_2016_midazolam"))
stopifnot(is.null(mod$linCmt))
p <- mod$theta
qh_scenario <- function(WT, scenario) {
  co <- (9119 - exp(9.164 - 2.9e-2 * WT + 3.91e-4 * WT^2 - 1.91e-6 * WT^3)) / 1000
  switch(scenario, 3.75 * WT^0.75 / 60, 0.25 * co, 0.25 * 7)
}
qh_tab <- tidyr::expand_grid(scenario = 1:3, WT = c(144, 98)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    qh_model = mapply(qh_scenario, WT, scenario),
    # Fig. 4 and Supplementary Information S1 (L/min)
    qh_published = c(2.6, 2.0, 1.9, 1.3, 1.75, 1.75)
  )
knitr::kable(qh_tab, digits = 3)
clint_ratio <- exp(p[["lcl_int_h_postsurg"]] - p[["lcl_int_h_presurg"]])
clint_ratio
stopifnot(
  abs(clint_ratio - 1.52) < 0.01,
  all(abs(qh_tab$qh_model - qh_tab$qh_published) < 0.06)
)
```

The model's scenario-1 flow at 98 kg is 1.95 L/min, which Supplementary
Information S1 prints as 2.0 L/min.

## Plasma clearance, FH and FG by scenario

Figure 4 shows the individual midazolam plasma clearance (Eq. 7), FH and FG
for each blood-flow scenario, and the Results give the median change after
surgery: plasma clearance x 1.28, 1.34 and 1.33, and FH x 0.84, 0.83 and
0.88, for scenarios 1-3. The table evaluates the same equations for a
typical 144 kg patient before and 98 kg patient after surgery, with the
CLint,H estimates the Results report for each scenario (16.9 / 25.6,
17.1 / 25.7 and 12.6 / 18.9 L/min) and the other parameters of Table 3.

```{r scenarios}
fig4 <- function(WT, scenario, cl_int_h) {
  qh <- qh_scenario(WT, scenario)
  qvi <- 0.6 * 0.8 * 0.4 * qh
  qgut <- qvi * 0.1766 / (qvi + 0.1766)
  eh <- cl_int_h * 0.033 / (qh + cl_int_h * 0.033)
  c(
    clplasma = qh * 0.033 * cl_int_h / (qh + 0.033 * cl_int_h / 0.66), # Eq. 7
    fh = 1 - eh,
    fg = 1 - 0.0199 / (qgut + 0.0199)
  )
}
clint_scen <- list(c(16.9, 25.6), c(17.1, 25.7), c(12.6, 18.9))
scen <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(1:3, function(s) {
  before <- fig4(144, s, clint_scen[[s]][1])
  after <- fig4(98, s, clint_scen[[s]][2])
  tibble::tibble(
    scenario = s,
    clplasma_before = before[["clplasma"]], clplasma_after = after[["clplasma"]],
    clplasma_ratio = after[["clplasma"]] / before[["clplasma"]],
    clplasma_ratio_published = c(1.28, 1.34, 1.33)[s],
    fh_ratio = after[["fh"]] / before[["fh"]],
    fh_ratio_published = c(0.84, 0.83, 0.88)[s],
    fg_before = before[["fg"]], fg_after = after[["fg"]]
  )
}))
knitr::kable(scen, digits = 3)
blood_cl_ratio_s1 <- {
  b <- fig4(144, 1, 16.9)
  a <- fig4(98, 1, 25.6)
  (1 - a[["fh"]]) * qh_scenario(98, 1) / ((1 - b[["fh"]]) * qh_scenario(144, 1))
}
blood_cl_ratio_s1
stopifnot(
  # Deterministic: same equations, same parameters as the paper.
  abs(scen$fh_ratio[1] - 0.84) < 0.02,
  abs(scen$clplasma_ratio[3] - 1.33) < 0.02,
  abs(blood_cl_ratio_s1 - 1.28) < 0.02
)
```

For scenario 3 (one blood flow for everyone) and for FH in scenario 1 the
typical-patient ratios match the published medians. The Eq. 7 plasma
clearance ratios of scenarios 1 and 2 (1.21 and 1.10) are lower than
published (1.28 and 1.34). For scenario 1 the ratio of the *blood*
clearances (`eh * qh`), printed below the table, is 1.28, the published
value; for scenarios 2 and 3 it is 1.18 and 1.37, so no single formula
reproduces all three published ratios. The published values are medians of
individual post hoc estimates over patients whose weights spread around the
medians, and in scenario 2 the blood flow changes steeply with weight, so a
typical-patient calculation only approximates them. The cohort simulation
below repeats the scenario-1 comparison with individual weights and random
effects.

# Mass balance and closed forms

With the organs at quasi-steady state, the model has exact closed forms for
the typical patient. After an IV dose all midazolam is eliminated by the
liver, so `AUC = Dose / (eh * qh)` in blood; after an oral dose the systemic
availability is `(1 - egut) * (1 - eh)`. All 1-OH-midazolam formed (from the
whole dose) is cleared by the liver with blood clearance `eh_1ohm * qh` after
passing the hepatic (and, for gut-formed metabolite, gut-wall) extraction
on its way out. These identities check the ODE wiring of the gut wall,
portal vein and liver against Eqs. 1-6.

```{r closed-form}
mod0 <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)
grid <- c(0, exp(seq(log(0.01), log(60000), length.out = 4000)))
closed_form <- function(WT, post) {
  qh <- 3.75 * WT^0.75 / 60
  qvi <- 0.6 * 0.8 * 0.4 * qh
  qgut <- qvi * 0.1766 / (qvi + 0.1766)
  clh <- exp(if (post == 1) p[["lcl_int_h_postsurg"]] else p[["lcl_int_h_presurg"]])
  eh <- clh * 0.033 / (qh + clh * 0.033)
  eg <- exp(p[["lcl_int_g"]]) / (qgut + exp(p[["lcl_int_g"]]))
  clm <- exp(p[["lcl_int_h_1ohm"]])
  egm_cl <- exp(p[["lcl_int_g_1ohm"]])
  ehm <- clm * 0.106 / (qh + clm * 0.106)
  egm <- egm_cl / (qvi + egm_cl)
  c(
    auc_iv = 5000 / (eh * qh),
    auc_po = 7500 * (1 - eg) * (1 - eh) / (eh * qh),
    auc_1ohm_iv = 5000 * (1 - ehm) / (ehm * qh),
    auc_1ohm_po = 7500 * (eg * (1 - egm) + (1 - eg)) * (1 - ehm) / (ehm * qh)
  )
}
trap <- function(t, y) sum(diff(t) * (head(y, -1) + tail(y, -1)) / 2)
one_dose <- function(amt, cmt, WT, post) {
  ev <- dplyr::bind_rows(
    data.frame(id = 1, time = 0, amt = amt, evid = 1, cmt = cmt, dvid = NA_integer_),
    data.frame(id = 1, time = grid, amt = 0, evid = 0, cmt = NA_character_, dvid = 1L)
  )
  ev$WT <- WT
  ev$PRIOR_BARIATRIC <- post
  as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod0, ev, maxsteps = 1e6))
}
cf_tab <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(list(c(144, 0), c(98, 1)), function(s) {
  iv <- one_dose(5000, "central", s[1], s[2])
  po <- one_dose(7500, "depot", s[1], s[2])
  cf <- closed_form(s[1], s[2])
  tibble::tibble(
    patient = c("144 kg, before surgery", "98 kg, after surgery")[s[2] + 1],
    quantity = names(cf),
    ode = c(trap(iv$time, iv$Cc), trap(po$time, po$Cc),
            trap(iv$time, iv$Cc_1ohm), trap(po$time, po$Cc_1ohm)),
    closed_form = unname(cf)
  )
})) |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (ode / closed_form - 1))
knitr::kable(cf_tab, digits = c(0, 0, 1, 1, 3))
# Same parameters on both sides: the difference is numerical error only.
stopifnot(all(abs(cf_tab$pct_diff) < 0.5))
```

# Virtual cohort

Two hundred virtual patients are studied before and one year after surgery,
as in the study. Pre-surgery weight is drawn from the Table 2 distribution
(144.4 +/- 21.7 kg) and the weight loss from 44.5 +/- 10.2 kg; draws outside
the observed ranges (112-186 kg before, 62-138 kg after, 21-58 kg loss) are
redrawn rather than truncated. Each patient receives 7.5 mg oral midazolam
and 5 mg IV midazolam 160 min later at each occasion. The two occasions sit
in one subject record so that the random effects are shared, as in the
model; the second occasion starts two weeks after the first, long enough
for midazolam and 1-OH-midazolam to be eliminated.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(2016)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(2016)
n_pt <- 200
draw_in <- function(n, mean, sd, lo, hi) {
  x <- rnorm(n, mean, sd)
  while (any(bad <- x < lo | x > hi)) x[bad] <- rnorm(sum(bad), mean, sd)
  x
}
pre_wt <- draw_in(n_pt, 144.4, 21.7, 112, 186)
loss <- draw_in(n_pt, 44.5, 10.2, 21, 58)
post_wt <- pre_wt - loss
while (any(bad <- post_wt < 62 | post_wt > 138)) {
  pre_wt[bad] <- draw_in(sum(bad), 144.4, 21.7, 112, 186)
  loss[bad] <- draw_in(sum(bad), 44.5, 10.2, 21, 58)
  post_wt <- pre_wt - loss
}
pts <- tibble::tibble(id = seq_len(n_pt), WT_pre = pre_wt, WT_post = post_wt)

occ2_start <- 20160 # two weeks, in min
obs_times <- c(5, 10, 15, 20, 30, 45, 60, 75, 90, 105, 120, 140, 160,
               160 + c(2, 5, 10, 15, 30, 45, 60, 90, 120, 180, 240, 300, 360,
                       480, 600, 720, 1440))
occasion_rows <- function(offset, post) {
  pts |>
    dplyr::mutate(WT = if (post == 1) WT_post else WT_pre, PRIOR_BARIATRIC = post) |>
    tidyr::crossing(tibble::tibble(
      time = offset + c(0, 160, obs_times),
      amt = c(7500, 5000, rep(0, length(obs_times))),
      evid = c(1L, 1L, rep(0L, length(obs_times))),
      cmt = c("depot", "central", rep(NA_character_, length(obs_times))),
      dvid = c(NA_integer_, NA_integer_, rep(1L, length(obs_times)))
    ))
}
ev_cohort <- dplyr::bind_rows(occasion_rows(0, 0), occasion_rows(occ2_start, 1)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, evid, cmt, dvid, WT, PRIOR_BARIATRIC) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid)) |>
  as.data.frame()

sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev_cohort, returnType = "data.frame",
                       maxsteps = 1e6) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    occasion = factor(ifelse(PRIOR_BARIATRIC == 1, "After surgery", "Before surgery"),
                      levels = c("Before surgery", "After surgery")),
    tad = ifelse(PRIOR_BARIATRIC == 1, time - occ2_start, time)
  )
```

## Concentration-time profiles

The paper shows goodness-of-fit plots rather than profiles (Figure 2b); the
figure below shows the model's typical profile and 5th-95th percentile band
for the study design, for both analytes.

```{r profiles, fig.height = 6}
sim |>
  dplyr::select(id, occasion, tad, Midazolam = Cc, `1-OH-midazolam` = Cc_1ohm) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(Midazolam, `1-OH-midazolam`), names_to = "analyte",
                      values_to = "conc") |>
  dplyr::group_by(analyte, occasion, tad) |>
  dplyr::summarise(lo = quantile(conc, 0.05), mid = median(conc),
                   hi = quantile(conc, 0.95), .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(tad, mid, colour = occasion, fill = occasion)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), alpha = 0.2, colour = NA) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~analyte, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time after oral dose (min)", y = "Blood concentration (ng/mL)",
       colour = NULL, fill = NULL,
       caption = paste("7.5 mg oral at 0 min, 5 mg IV at 160 min.\nLines: median;",
                       "bands: 5th-95th percentile of 200 virtual patients.")) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11)
```

## Replicating Figures 3 and 4

Figure 3 compares the individual CLint,H and CLint,G before and after
surgery, and Figure 4 the derived plasma clearance, FH and FG. The panels
below draw the same quantities for the virtual cohort (scenario 1).

```{r fig3-4, fig.height = 6}
indiv <- sim |>
  dplyr::group_by(id, occasion) |>
  dplyr::slice(1) |>
  dplyr::ungroup() |>
  dplyr::mutate(clplasma = qh * 0.033 * cl_int_h / (qh + 0.033 * cl_int_h / 0.66)) # Eq. 7
indiv |>
  dplyr::select(occasion, `CLint,H (L/min)` = cl_int_h, `CLint,G (L/min)` = cl_int_g,
                `Plasma CL (L/min)` = clplasma, FH = fhep, FG = fgut) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-occasion) |>
  ggplot(aes(occasion, value, fill = occasion)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.6) +
  facet_wrap(~name, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("grey20", "grey70")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = NULL,
       caption = "Replicates Figures 3 and 4 (scenario 1) of Brill 2016 for 200 virtual patients.") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

fig4_cohort <- indiv |>
  dplyr::group_by(occasion) |>
  dplyr::summarise(clplasma = median(clplasma), fh = median(fhep),
                   fg = median(fgut), .groups = "drop")
fig4_ratio <- c(
  clplasma = fig4_cohort$clplasma[2] / fig4_cohort$clplasma[1],
  fh = fig4_cohort$fh[2] / fig4_cohort$fh[1]
)
knitr::kable(fig4_cohort, digits = 3)
fig4_ratio
stopifnot(
  # Results: scenario 1 median decrease of FH 0.84 after surgery.
  abs(fig4_ratio[["fh"]] - 0.84) < 0.04,
  # Plasma clearance rises after surgery; the Eq. 7 ratio sits near the
  # typical-patient 1.21 (published 1.28, see the scenario table above).
  fig4_ratio[["clplasma"]] > 1.05 && fig4_ratio[["clplasma"]] < 1.45,
  # FG close to one in both groups (Figure 4, lower row).
  all(fig4_cohort$fg > 0.7)
)
```

The cohort reproduces the published decrease in FH and the high FG in both
groups. Its plasma-clearance ratio follows the typical-patient value of
about 1.21 rather than the published 1.28, as discussed above.

## Residual error by surgery stratum

The two strata have their own proportional residual SD, shared by both
analytes. The ratio of the simulated relative residuals checks that the
stratum switch reaches the error model.

```{r residual}
res_sd <- sim |>
  dplyr::group_by(occasion) |>
  dplyr::summarise(rel_sd = sd((sim / Cc - 1)[Cc > 0]), .groups = "drop")
res_sd
sd_ratio <- res_sd$rel_sd[2] / res_sd$rel_sd[1]
stopifnot(abs(sd_ratio / (0.237 / 0.326) - 1) < 0.1)
```

# PKNCA validation

Non-compartmental analysis of a separate 5 mg IV bolus simulation for the
same cohort, by occasion, out to 7 days so that the slow second peripheral
phase is captured. Concentrations below 0.01 ng/mL are set to missing: far
in the tail the ODE solution is round-off noise around zero (values of
+/-1e-11 ng/mL), which PKNCA cannot fit, and the AUC beyond that level is
negligible. Midazolam is cleared only by the liver, so each patient's
AUC from zero to infinity should equal the dose divided by that patient's
blood clearance `eh * qh`. The paper reports no NCA results, so the check is
against the model's own individual clearances.

```{r pknca}
iv_grid <- c(0, exp(seq(log(1), log(10080), length.out = 120)))
iv_rows <- function(post) {
  pts |>
    dplyr::mutate(WT = if (post == 1) WT_post else WT_pre, PRIOR_BARIATRIC = post,
                  id = id + post * n_pt) |>
    tidyr::crossing(tibble::tibble(
      time = c(0, iv_grid),
      amt = c(5000, rep(0, length(iv_grid))),
      evid = c(1L, rep(0L, length(iv_grid))),
      cmt = c("central", rep(NA_character_, length(iv_grid))),
      dvid = c(NA_integer_, rep(1L, length(iv_grid)))
    ))
}
ev_iv <- dplyr::bind_rows(iv_rows(0), iv_rows(1)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, evid, cmt, dvid, WT, PRIOR_BARIATRIC) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid)) |>
  as.data.frame()
sim_iv <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev_iv, returnType = "data.frame", maxsteps = 1e6) |>
  dplyr::mutate(occasion = ifelse(PRIOR_BARIATRIC == 1, "After surgery", "Before surgery"))

conc_iv <- sim_iv |>
  dplyr::mutate(Cc = ifelse(Cc < 0.01, NA_real_, Cc)) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, occasion)
dose_iv <- sim_iv |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, occasion) |>
  dplyr::mutate(time = 0, amt = 5000)
conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_iv, Cc ~ time | occasion + id,
                             concu = "ng/mL", timeu = "min")
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_iv, amt ~ time | occasion + id,
                             doseu = "ug", route = "intravascular")
intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, cmax = TRUE, aucinf.obs = TRUE,
                        half.life = TRUE, cl.obs = TRUE)
nca_iv <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
summary(nca_iv)

cl_indiv <- sim_iv |>
  dplyr::group_by(id) |>
  dplyr::slice(1) |>
  dplyr::ungroup() |>
  dplyr::transmute(id, auc_expected = 5000 / (eh * qh))
chk <- as.data.frame(nca_iv$result) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "aucinf.obs") |>
  dplyr::inner_join(cl_indiv, by = "id") |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (PPORRES / auc_expected - 1))
chk |>
  dplyr::group_by(occasion) |>
  dplyr::summarise(median_pct_diff = median(pct_diff),
                   p90_abs_pct_diff = quantile(abs(pct_diff), 0.9), .groups = "drop") |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)
stopifnot(
  # Structural: a mis-wired liver or a wrong dose moves every patient.
  abs(median(chk$pct_diff)) < 2,
  # Envelope: extrapolation over the slow peripheral phase varies by patient.
  quantile(abs(chk$pct_diff), 0.9) < 10
)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Second inter-compartmental clearance (Q2) not reported.** Table 3 has no
  row for it, and the text and supplements give no value. The authors' code
  estimates it (`Q12 = THETA(18)`, initial value 0.5 L/min); the model fixes
  it at that initial value. Q2 sets the exchange with the large second
  peripheral volume (Vp2 = 10.8 x Vp, about 335 L after surgery), so the late
  terminal phase of midazolam depends on this assumption. The final value
  has been requested from the authors.
* **Table 3 row 'Q2 = Q1 * A, A = 3.22 FIX'.** The code applies A to the
  first inter-compartmental clearance after surgery
  (`IF(OBES.EQ.2) TVQ = THETA(2)*THETA(24) ; fQ BA`), the Methods say a
  separate inter-compartmental clearance was used for the two groups, the
  footnote defines A as the "factor difference with morbidly obese
  patients", and 3.22 is the post-surgery factor on Q of Brill 2015. The
  model follows the code: Q = 1.41 L/min before and 4.54 L/min after
  surgery, and the row label is taken as a misprint.
* **Reference weight 127 kg.** Table 3 centres the weight effects on Vc and
  Vp at 144 kg; the code centres them at 127 kg, the median weight over both
  occasions and the reference at which Brill 2015 estimated X = 0.0435 and
  Y = 3.93. The model follows the code. Before surgery the linear Vc term
  becomes negative below 104 kg, outside the observed range of 112-186 kg.
* **Unbound fraction of midazolam in blood.** Table 1 prints fuB = 0.0303;
  the code and Supplementary Information S2 use 0.033. The model follows the
  code.
* **Hepatic blood flow in the Discussion.** The Discussion gives
  "QH = 3.7 L/min at 144 kg" for scenario 1, but the Table 1 equation gives
  2.6 L/min, which is what Figure 4 and Supplementary Information S1 print.
  The Discussion value is taken as a typo.
* **Scenario 1 only.** The paper presents the final estimates of hepatic
  blood flow scenario 1 (allometric flow); for scenarios 2 and 3 it reports
  only CLint,H and states that the other parameters were very similar. Only
  scenario 1 is packaged; the "Derived quantities" section shows the other
  two by their equations.
* **Blood concentrations.** The model was fitted to blood concentrations
  (Figure 2b, Table 3 "Blood parameter estimates", code comments "blood
  conc."). Midazolam plasma concentrations are the blood concentrations
  divided by the blood-to-plasma ratio of 0.66; for 1-OH-midazolam the ratio
  is 1.
* **Metabolite mass.** The code applies no molecular-weight conversion, so
  1-OH-midazolam concentrations are in midazolam-mass equivalents (the
  molecular weights are about 326 and 342 g/mol).
* **IIV scale.** The paper reports IIV as % CV without a formula; the
  variances are `log(1 + CV^2)`, as in the other Leiden midazolam models in
  this package. This matters most for CLint,G (493% CV, variance 3.23); if
  the authors' % CV is `100 * sqrt(omega^2)`, the variance would be 24.3.
  No IIV was estimated on Q, Q2 or any 1-OH-midazolam parameter.
* **Random effects shared by both occasions.** The paper estimated no
  inter-occasion variability.
* **IV administration.** The paper does not give the duration of the IV
  dose; simulations give it as a bolus into the central compartment.
* **Poorly identified metabolite gut-wall clearance.** CLint,G,1-OH has an
  RSE of 180% and a bootstrap mean of 4.7e22 L/min; the Results report that
  excluding two patients changes it to 6.7 L/min. The model uses the Table 3
  estimate of 11.9 L/min.
* **CLint,H values.** Table 3 gives 16.8 and 25.5 L/min; the Results text
  gives 16.9 and 25.6 L/min for the same scenario. The model uses Table 3.
